page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average range, supported by Intel AVX-512 vector extensions. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, are positioned in the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations also register in the bottom quartile, which impacts data-intensive tasks.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.hfg6.xlarge offers dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute performance without noisy-neighbor interference. However, the tradeoff is lower overall throughput in highly parallelized workloads, as evidenced by weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and database operation scores. This profile is best suited for general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand high memory bandwidth or local storage, such as lightweight web serving, basic text processing, or small-scale application hosting.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, running on a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. It delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data shows average single-core performance, aided by AVX-512 instruction support, but reveals weaker multi-core scaling and lower memory bandwidth. Consequently, the ecs.hfg6.xlarge is best suited for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation with moderate compute needs, such as lightweight web serving, text processing, and basic application hosting, rather than memory-intensive or highly parallelized database operations.
